A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 82-page paper, including Appendices A–J. Complete text and rendered-page comparisons identify differences only in the arXiv stamp and one sentence in Theorem 3; all other pages match.

before.justification: v4 reports original SSM training simulations and synthetic and CIFAR-10 clean-label poisoning experiments in Section 4 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the dynamical-characterization plots and poisoning results in Section 4 and Appendix I.

M1.justification: The SSM formulation, training objectives, gradient-flow dynamics and experimental poisoning procedures are identical in Sections 2–4 and Appendix J.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic teacher-student sequence tasks and sequential CIFAR-10 poisoning scenarios, including all Appendix I variants.

E2.justification: The same clean-training controls accompany each poisoning experiment. Evaluated model configurations and comparison membership are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E3.justification: Data construction, sample sizes, sequence lengths, metrics, model dimensions and optimization settings remain identical in Section 4 and Appendix J.

E4.justification: Appendix I retains the same parameter-dynamics, effective-rank and gamma analyses, higher-dimensional-teacher investigations and training-performance controls. No analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both report synthetic poisoning results averaged over four random seeds and CIFAR-10 results over three. Standard-deviation reporting in Tables 4, 5, 7 and 8 is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match. For example, Table 2 reports S4 test accuracy of 78.8% without poisoning and 76.9% with poisoning in both PDFs; appendix results also remain identical.

T1.justification: Appendix F.3.3, Theorem 3, changes 'analytic (i.e. C∞) vector field' to 'analytic vector field.' This corrects the false equivalence between analyticity and infinite differentiability while retaining the analytic hypothesis. The remaining theorem statement and surrounding proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about SSM learning dynamics and susceptibility to clean-label poisoning.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations and Section 5 limitations are unchanged, including restricted theoretical settings, initialization-set size, near-zero initialization and limited experimental scale.

D1.justification: Appendix J and Tables 9–19 retain the same implementation, hardware, data-processing, initialization, hyperparameter and training details. Code-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography, related-work discussion and novelty positioning are identical, including Appendix A and Theorem 3's existing source attribution.

P1.justification: Theorem 3 loses one parenthetical, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. All other prose, section ordering and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions and placements are unchanged. The theorem edit causes only incidental wrapping within the same paragraph, with no change to page organization or display structure.

improvement.justification: Removing '(i.e. C∞)' from Theorem 3 corrects a mathematical misstatement and makes its analyticity assumption unambiguous. This provides a limited improvement in precision; the main results, surrounding proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
